timeZh: t ≈ 大爆炸后 3 分钟
tagZh: 最初三分钟：宇宙写下了氢与氦的第一行诗。
tagEn: The first three minutes: the universe wrote its opening line in hydrogen and helium.
narrativeZh: 宇宙诞生后的最初三分钟，温度降至十亿开尔文，质子与中子在炽热的等离子汤中结合——氢与氦就此铸成，至今仍占宇宙普通物质的 98%。（原初核合成也留下了一丝锂，但今天宇宙中的锂大多另有来源，故本馆将它归入宇宙射线散裂。）此后的一切，都从这两种原料开始。
narrativeEn: In the first three minutes, as temperatures fell to a billion kelvin, protons and neutrons bonded in the primordial plasma—hydrogen and helium were cast, and they still make up 98% of all ordinary matter. (A whisper of lithium was made too, but most lithium today has other origins, so this exhibit files it under cosmic-ray spallation.) Everything since began with these two ingredients.

tagZh: 巨星在爆炸中死去，把氧与钙赠予未来的生命。
tagEn: Giant stars die in explosions, bequeathing oxygen and calcium to life yet to come.
narrativeZh: 超新星爆发之一：核坍缩超新星。第一代大质量恒星点亮黑暗时代，在数百万年间烧穿氢、氦、碳、氖、氧、硅，直到铁核坍缩——爆炸把氧、镁、硅、钙抛向星际，为行星与生命铺路。
narrativeEn: Supernova explosion, part one: core collapse. The first massive stars lit the cosmic dark ages, burning through hydrogen, helium, carbon, neon, oxygen and silicon in mere millions of years until their iron cores collapsed—the blast hurled oxygen, magnesium, silicon and calcium into space, paving the way for planets and life.

tagZh: 白矮星的热核烈焰，铸造了你血液中的铁。
tagEn: A white dwarf's thermonuclear fire forged the iron in your blood.
narrativeZh: 超新星爆发之二：热核超新星。一颗白矮星从伴星窃取物质，逼近钱德拉塞卡极限，整颗恒星在热核失控中炸裂——Ia 型超新星。没有残骸留下，只有约半个太阳质量的放射性镍，衰变成宇宙中大部分的铁。
narrativeEn: Supernova explosion, part two: thermonuclear. A white dwarf steals matter from its companion, nears the Chandrasekhar limit and detonates in runaway fusion—a Type Ia supernova. No remnant survives, only about half a solar mass of radioactive nickel that decays into most of the universe's iron.

tagZh: 太阳的同类在暮年缓缓呼出碳、氮与铅。
tagEn: Stars like our Sun exhale carbon, nitrogen and lead in their twilight.
narrativeZh: 中低质量恒星的死亡。像太阳一样的恒星步入暮年，膨胀为红巨星。在脉动的氦壳层中，慢中子俘获过程耐心地一个中子一个中子地堆砌出锶、钡、铅，再随恒星风化作行星状星云，把碳与氮散入银河。
narrativeEn: The death of intermediate- and low-mass stars. Sun-like stars age into red giants. In their pulsing helium shells the slow neutron-capture process patiently builds strontium, barium and lead one neutron at a time; then stellar winds bloom into planetary nebulae, seeding the Galaxy with carbon and nitrogen.

timeEn: From the first supernovae until today
tagZh: 在星际虚空中，宇宙射线把原子核击碎成锂、铍与硼。
tagEn: In the interstellar void, cosmic rays shatter nuclei into lithium, beryllium and boron.
narrativeZh: 超新星遗迹把粒子加速到近光速，成为宇宙射线。当它们撞击星际气体中的碳、氮、氧原子核，碎裂的残片就是锂、铍和硼——恒星核心无法保存的三种轻元素，只能在星际虚空中被「击碎」出来。
narrativeEn: Supernova remnants accelerate particles to near light speed as cosmic rays. When they strike carbon, nitrogen and oxygen nuclei in interstellar gas, the shattered fragments are lithium, beryllium and boron—three light elements no stellar core can preserve, which only the void can break into being.

timeEn: Hundreds of millions of years onward
tagZh: 两颗死星相撞的千分之一秒，铸成了黄金。
tagEn: A millisecond of two dead stars colliding forged the gold.
narrativeZh: 两颗中子星在引力波的挽歌中旋转靠近、相撞。千分之一秒内，海量中子被原子核吞噬——快中子俘获过程铸成金、铂、铀。2017 年 8 月 17 日，人类首次目睹了这场宇宙炼金术。
narrativeEn: Two neutron stars spiral together in a gravitational-wave requiem and collide. In milliseconds, nuclei swallow floods of neutrons—the rapid capture process forges gold, platinum and uranium. On 17 August 2017, humanity witnessed this cosmic alchemy for the first time.

tagZh: 星尘学会了铸造新的星尘。
tagEn: Starstuff has learned to forge new starstuff.
narrativeZh: 1937 年，人类在回旋加速器中造出锝——第一个不存在于地球自然界的元素。此后，反应堆与加速器一个原子一个原子地推进周期表，直到第 118 号元素。星尘，开始自己铸造元素。
narrativeEn: In 1937 humans made technetium in a cyclotron—the first element absent from nature on Earth. Since then, reactors and accelerators have pushed the table forward atom by atom to element 118. Starstuff has begun to forge elements of its own.

tagZh: 一百一十八种元素，七座宇宙熔炉——我们由星尘铸成。
tagEn: One hundred and eighteen elements, seven cosmic furnaces—we are made of starstuff.
narrativeZh: 七种宇宙熔炉，一百一十八种元素。从大爆炸的氢到实验室的鿫，每一个格子都是一段跨越亿万年的旅程。我们由星尘铸成——而今天，星尘正凝视着自己。
narrativeEn: Seven cosmic furnaces, one hundred and eighteen elements. From Big Bang hydrogen to laboratory oganesson, every tile is a journey across the aeons. We are made of starstuff—and today, the starstuff is looking back at itself.
